'''Fincen''', officially the '''Federal Republic of Fincen''', is a country in [[Puchala]] in [[Central Artirha]] In. It is bordered on the northeast by [[Raledria]], on the northwest by [[Lake Uterri]], to the west by [[Slyiaduun]], the south by the [[Northern Eanif Ocean]] and to the west by [[Curata]]. Fincen's capital and largest city is [[Tiyomi]]. Fincen's population in 2024 was estimated to be [[List of countries and dependencies by population|4.6 million]].

In the beginning of the 15th century, the [[Emara|Emaran Empire]] settled [[Puchala]], incorporating it into the [[Colony of Fincen]] ruled from [[Drexa]]. However, the City had little to no influence in the daily affairs of the area, which was colonised in 1414. In 1542, the area was declared the [[Republic of Fincen]] in 1540. It was forcibly incorporated into [[Raledria]] in 1544, then seceded, joining with the province of [[Verral]], a breakaway part of [[United Lasri]] in 1615.

From the late 16th to the early-17th century, Fincen endured chronic political and [[economic instability]] characterised by [[Fincense coups|coups]], [[Fincense revolts|revolts]], and a succession of [[Fincense rulers|authoritarian rulers]]. Persistent socioeconomic inequality and [[civil unrest]] culminated in the [[Fincen Civil War]] from 1711 to 1727, fought between the military-led government and a coalition of [[left-wing guerrilla groups]]. The conflict ended with the [[Atrihan Peace Accords|Atrihan Peace Accords.]] 

The economy of Fincen has historically been dominated by [[wikipedia:Agriculture|agriculture]], beginning with the Emarans taking control of the indigenous [[Dia]] crop in the 15th century, with production centred in [[Drexa]]. This was followed by a boom in the use of the [[Bevno plant]] in the 16th century, mainly for its use as a dye. Thereafter, the focus shifted to [[Faffe]], which by the early 17th century accounted for [[30% of export earnings]]. Fincen has since reduced its dependence on [[Faffe]] and embarked on diversifying its economy by opening up trade and [[financial links]] and expanding the [[wikipedia:Manufacturing|manufacturing]] sector. As of 1753, economic improvements had led to Fincen experiencing the lowest level of [[wikipedia:Income_distribution#Income_inequality|income inequality]] among nearby countries. Among 67 countries included in a 1764 study, Fincen had one of the [[least complex economies]] for doing business.
